variants.title: The Last Measure of Grain
variants.summary: A household store is nearly empty, and two families have been promised the same remaining grain. The steward needs a count before anyone receives less than they were told.
variants.dialogue: The bins will not fill themselves. Count what remains with me, then tell each household what we can actually spare.
objectives: Check the remaining grain against the households' declared needs and record the shortfall.
Deliver the agreed portions to the named households, obtaining acknowledgment without pretending the shortage is over.
variants.alternate: If the promised grain is unavailable, offer a smaller witnessed distribution with the households' consent and record who still needs aid.
variants.failure: An unrecorded diversion or a claim that all households were supplied closes the request without relief credit.

variants.title: The Wet Grain Sacks
variants.summary: A seller opens a sack of damp grain after buyers have paid for sound provisions. Passing it off as dry would leave households with spoiled food.
variants.dialogue: I promised sound grain, not these clumped kernels. Help me set the measure right before the buyers return.
objectives: Inspect the affected sacks and record the usable weight against the paid market order.
Arrange sound replacement provisions through the local market, then deliver the agreed amount to the named buyers.
variants.alternate: If sound grain is unobtainable, offer a buyer-approved alternative staple or refund the unsupplied portion at its actual price.
variants.failure: The paid order remains unsettled; damp goods must not be certified as sound provisions.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Source a scarce staple; inspect quality before delivery.

variants.title: Two Claims on the Last Sack
variants.summary: Two buyers each have a marked promise for the same remaining market stock. The seller cannot honor both claims without deciding what the records actually establish.
variants.dialogue: Both have my mark, and both say they were first. The last sack cannot be in two kitchens at once.
objectives: Compare the buyers' promises with the seller's dated tally and weigh the stock actually available.
Record an allocation or refund accepted by the affected buyers before handing over the disputed goods.
variants.alternate: If priority cannot be proven, seek agreement on a divided allotment and a corrected price, or suspend the sale rather than choose a claimant by rumor.
variants.failure: The disputed order closes without an agreed allocation; no claimant receives goods as though the other claim had vanished.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Source a scarce staple; inspect quality before delivery.

variants.title: Provisions Before Departure
variants.summary: A party of travelers is preparing to leave, but the vendor has discovered that its reserved rations will not cover the journey. Spoiled substitutes would put the party at risk beyond the market.
variants.dialogue: They leave at first light. If I fill their packs with poor food, they will discover the mistake far from another stall.
objectives: Check the travelers' reserved provisions for soundness and compare the quantity with their stated journey.
Obtain a safe market allotment and hand it over before departure, recording any shortfall with the party.
variants.alternate: If the agreed ration is unavailable, offer the travelers a smaller safe supply and the choice to delay departure or reclaim their advance.
variants.failure: The departure order is not fulfilled; unsafe or missing rations cannot be treated as a completed delivery.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Source a scarce staple; inspect quality before delivery.

variants.title: The Empty Staple Stall
variants.summary: The market's usual food seller has only damaged sacks left. A replacement shipment may arrive too late for the households buying their daily provisions.
variants.dialogue: I can pay for good grain, not damp chaff. Show me the weight and the condition before I open the market purse.
objectives: Inspect available staple stocks and compare their sound weight and asking price.
Purchase an agreed wholesome allotment through the current market and document its delivery to the stall.
variants.alternate: If the named staple cannot be bought, present another locally accepted food staple with its true quantity and price for the market keeper's approval.
variants.failure: Passing spoiled goods as sound stock or concealing a higher purchase price forfeits the commission.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Source a scarce staple; inspect quality before delivery.

variants.title: The Unclaimed Packet
variants.summary: A sealed instruction has reached its destination, but the receiving clerk is absent and no one will acknowledge custody. Reaching the town is not the same as delivering the packet.
variants.dialogue: The desk is empty. I need a name beside this seal, not an assurance that someone must have seen it.
objectives: Check the addressee and intact seal against the issuing clerk's dispatch record.
Hand the packet to its named recipient or an authorized deputy and obtain a receipt; otherwise return it unopened.
variants.alternate: If there is no authorized recipient, return the sealed packet to the issuing clerk with an account of the attempted delivery.
variants.failure: Leaving an unreceipted packet or breaking its seal cannot be counted as a valid delivery.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Carry a sealed dispatch; obtain a valid receipt or return it intact.

variants.title: Conflicting Orders
variants.summary: Two clerks hold differently sealed instructions covering the same errand. Their disagreement is not proof that either instruction is forged.
variants.dialogue: Keep both seals intact. We must learn which office issued each order before anyone acts on it.
objectives: Compare the issuing offices, dates, seals and named recipients without opening the packets.
Deliver only a verified instruction and obtain a receipt naming the packet and its recipient.
variants.alternate: If either order cannot be authenticated, return it intact for clarification rather than accuse a clerk without evidence.
variants.failure: Delivering an unauthenticated order or claiming an accusation is proof voids the disputed commission.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Carry a sealed dispatch; obtain a valid receipt or return it intact.

variants.title: The Changing Watch Roster
variants.summary: The watch is being reassigned while its next patrol's sealed instruction remains with the messenger. The departing officer's receipt would not establish that the incoming patrol was informed.
variants.dialogue: The old watch is leaving. Find the officer taking duty before this order disappears between the shifts.
objectives: Confirm the incoming receiving officer against the watch clerk's current roster and check the sealed instruction.
Deliver to the officer actually taking duty and obtain an acknowledgment tied to that roster.
variants.alternate: If the receiving officer cannot be established, return the packet to the watch clerk for redirection.
variants.failure: Passing the instruction to an unidentified guard or relying on an outgoing officer's receipt does not establish handover.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Carry a sealed dispatch; obtain a valid receipt or return it intact.

variants.title: No Horse for the Seal
variants.summary: The official courier's mount has gone lame before a sealed order can leave town. The issuing clerk will not trust an unnamed messenger.
variants.dialogue: The seal stays whole, even if the road is slow. Bring me a witness to the handover or bring the letter back.
objectives: Confirm the seal and destination with the issuing clerk before taking custody.
Deliver the unopened packet to its named recipient and obtain an acknowledgment, or return it intact.
variants.alternate: If no credible courier or safe route is available, return the unbroken dispatch to the issuing clerk for a recorded delay.
variants.failure: A broken seal without authority, a false receipt or a lost dispatch ends the commission without payment.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Carry a sealed dispatch; obtain a valid receipt or return it intact.

variants.title: The Caravan That Cannot Depart
variants.summary: A small traveling party has lost a guard and cannot cross the reported dangerous stretch as planned. Waiting costs provisions, but a hurried departure risks lives.
variants.dialogue: We cannot march with an empty watch. Show us a route we can defend, or help us wait until the next company gathers.
objectives: Meet the travelers, confirm their destination and the actual guard and provision shortfall.
Escort them across an agreed safe segment, accounting for losses and the route taken.
variants.alternate: If an adequate escort is unavailable, agree to delay departure or take a witnessed safer detour rather than falsely declaring the road secure.
variants.failure: Abandoning the party in the declared danger or claiming an untraveled route earns no escort reward.

variants.title: The Witness Who Left
variants.summary: One of the witnesses to a disputed incident has departed and the remaining accounts contradict each other. A mark at the scene may be the only evidence that can still be checked.
variants.dialogue: I will not put a name in the record on the strength of gossip. Find what can still be seen.
objectives: Inspect the scene and record which physical traces remain reliable.
Compare the available independent accounts, separating what was seen from what was repeated.
variants.alternate: If a key witness cannot be found, preserve the surviving evidence and explicitly leave the disputed allegation unresolved.
variants.failure: Presenting rumor as a sworn observation invalidates the inquiry and forfeits its reward.

variants.title: A Workshop Without Its Tools
variants.summary: A working family has lost a necessary set of tools and cannot afford an unverified replacement. Another claim of ownership has surfaced at the market.
variants.dialogue: I can recognize my maker's mark. Do not buy back my own tools from a stranger without asking me first.
objectives: Trace the missing tools and compare maker's marks or other ownership evidence.
Return the tools to the rightful household or arrange an agreed equivalent remedy with a witnessed handover.
variants.alternate: If the original tools are gone, seek the owner's consent to a serviceable replacement or fair compensation; record the unresolved loss.
variants.failure: Delivering unusable equipment or transferring disputed tools without establishing ownership ends the recovery without credit.

variants.title: Beyond the Last Known Track
variants.summary: A guide knows the approach to an uncharted stretch, but the survey party lacks enough provisions to verify the far side. An incomplete map could mislead later travelers.
variants.dialogue: Draw only what your feet and eyes can defend. Leave the unknown ground blank for the next party.
objectives: Agree on a safe bounded survey route with the guide and check available provisions.
Record observed landmarks and return with clear distinctions between visited ground and unverified reports.
variants.alternate: If provisions will not cover the full traverse, survey the reachable approaches and mark the unsurveyed extent as unknown, without revealing unseen sites.
variants.failure: Invented landmarks or a map that presents hearsay as direct observation invalidates the survey.

variants.dialogue: The apprentice may learn from a mistake, but the customer must not pay for it. Bring me material I can approve.
objectives: Identify the missing material and the workmanship standard with the master.
Acquire suitable stock and complete a supervised trial piece that the master can inspect.
variants.alternate: If the usual stock is exhausted, obtain the master's approval for a proven alternative material and document any changed limits of use.
variants.failure: Passing a weak trial piece or an unapproved substitute as finished work forfeits the workshop commission.

variants.title: One Watchman at the Gate
variants.summary: The watch has too few patrols to cover a suspected nighttime approach. An unguarded arrest attempt could warn the whole group or harm bystanders.
variants.dialogue: One frightened witness is not a gang. Watch the gate and bring me signs I can act upon.
objectives: Observe the named approach discreetly and distinguish witnessed activity from accusation.
Report corroborated movements to the watch and support an authorized warning or arrest where safe.
variants.alternate: If no safe patrol is available, warn the watch of the uncovered approach and maintain an observed report without attempting an unauthorized lone arrest.
variants.failure: A false accusation or an unsupported seizure closes the watch request without reward.

variants.title: The Garrison's Short Measure
variants.summary: An outpost requisition exceeds the serviceable stores on hand. Its captain needs an honest issue account more than a crate of unsuitable equipment.
variants.dialogue: Do not count broken gear as arms fit for duty. Tell me what can be issued now and what remains missing.
objectives: Check the requisition against inspected stores and separate serviceable equipment from damaged goods.
Issue the approved allotment to the defenders and witness the shortage recorded on the store ledger.
variants.alternate: If the full requisition cannot be supplied, deliver only the approved serviceable portion and record the unmet quantity for later issue.
variants.failure: Concealing a short delivery or supplying condemned equipment as serviceable voids the stores commission.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Audit the request; deliver serviceable supplies and witness their issue.

variants.title: The Jammed Halyard
variants.summary: An outbound trader cannot lower a yard because its halyard is caught in a split wooden block. The master wants the berth cleared, but the boatswain will not let the crew haul against a jammed fitting.
variants.dialogue: Hear that crack when they haul? That block is splitting. Give me a sound one and I'll show you whether the yard moves free.
objectives: Examine the jammed halyard and identify whether the block or the rope is unsafe to reuse.
Fit a serviceable replacement, re-reeve the halyard and witness a controlled lowering-and-raising trial with the boatswain.
variants.alternate: If a safe block or line cannot be found, secure the yard and keep the vessel alongside; do not approve departure on the strength of a temporary knot.
variants.failure: Declaring the fouled rig safe without a working trial forfeits the commission and leaves the departure unresolved.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Restore a usable halyard with a witnessed trial before the trader's rig is cleared for service.

variants.title: The Spar the Shipwright Refused
variants.summary: A shipmaster wants to reuse a yard with an old split, while the shipwright says the timber will not bear another passage. Both demand a decision before the spare spar is issued.
variants.dialogue: The master sees a timber worth saving. I see the split running with the grain. Put it under inspection before either of us wagers a crew on it.
objectives: Inspect the disputed spar and compare its damage with the shipwright's recorded repair limits.
Secure a sound replacement if needed, rig it correctly and obtain a witnessed working trial before assigning responsibility for the delay.
variants.alternate: If a safe spar is unavailable, berth the vessel and record the unsatisfied repair rather than compelling either party to sign an unsafe clearance.
variants.failure: Approving a split spar without the shipwright's test ends the job without fleet stores or a valid repair record.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Resolve the contested spar against a witnessed rigging trial rather than a captain's unsupported clearance.

variants.title: The Slack Shrouds
variants.summary: A squall has loosened a vessel's mast shrouds while the crew prepares to leave. The rigger needs sound lanyards before the mast can take a safe load.
variants.dialogue: Watch the mast when the gust hits. If those shrouds pull loose under sail, we will be past choosing where to turn back.
objectives: Keep the vessel secured and inspect the shrouds, deadeyes and lanyards for the source of the slack.
Replace or re-tension serviceable rigging and witness a cautious load trial before authorizing departure.
variants.alternate: When suitable lanyards cannot be obtained, leave the ship moored until conditions and fittings permit a proper repair; no rushed clearance is acceptable.
variants.failure: Letting the vessel depart with unverified standing rigging forfeits the award and leaves the hazard uncorrected.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Restore safe mast support through inspected shrouds and a completed tension trial.

variants.title: The Lantern That Cannot Be Lit
variants.summary: A harbor signal and its fittings need repair before the next departure, but the usual spare parts are missing. A partial repair must not be mistaken for a safe signal.
variants.dialogue: A dark light is dangerous. A light that lies is worse. Test the fitting before anyone sails by it.
objectives: Inspect the signal or rigging defect and identify the fitting needed for safe operation.
Install approved serviceable parts and conduct a witnessed trial before declaring the signal usable.
variants.alternate: If a suitable fitting is unobtainable, leave the apparatus explicitly out of service and arrange a temporary warning rather than approving an unsafe trial.
variants.failure: Declaring an untested or unsafe light operational ends the commission without payment.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Restore the harbor's signal only after a serviceable fitting and witnessed trial establish that the light conveys a trustworthy warning.

variants.title: The Levy Entered Twice
variants.summary: A dues clerk has entered the same paid consignment on two collection lines. The carrier has one receipt, but a second demand is already headed to the household.
variants.dialogue: The marks look alike, but a similar mark does not settle a debt. Put the dates beside the receipt before I change the roll.
objectives: Compare the two levy entries with the payer's dated receipt and the original collector's mark.
Identify whether they represent one payment or two obligations, then record a witnessed correction without erasing the disputed entry.
variants.alternate: If the collector's record cannot be checked, mark the second demand as disputed and defer collection rather than inventing proof of payment.
variants.failure: Collecting a second time without evidence leaves the household wronged and the ledger challenge unresolved.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: A documented duplicate-charge correction reduces the risk of unjust collection and resulting unrest.

variants.title: Dues on the Shared Harvest
variants.summary: Two households brought in a shared harvest, but the dues roll names only one as liable. The collector wants a single debtor while both parties contest how the crop was divided.
variants.dialogue: I can enter what they actually shared. I cannot turn a season's harvest bargain into a judgment about who owns the field.
objectives: Hear both households separately and compare the harvest tally with the collector's stated assessment basis.
Record a witnessed interim division or identify the part still disputed, without rewriting permanent land rights.
variants.alternate: If neither party accepts the measured split, refer the disputed share for hearing while retaining the undisputed contribution in the roll.
variants.failure: Charging the whole levy to one household without examining the division aggravates the dispute and defeats the settlement.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: An evidenced interim harvest assessment reduces tension without turning a temporary dues ruling into a title judgment.

variants.title: The Collector Has Arrived
variants.summary: A collector is preparing to seize goods for arrears just as a household produces evidence of an earlier partial payment. Delay may make any later correction useless.
variants.dialogue: He may collect what the record supports. But if that receipt is genuine, we must not take the same portion again.
objectives: Check the household's receipt against the collector's demand and identify the amount actually outstanding.
Present the supported balance to the responsible clerk before collection, recording a stay of the disputed portion or a witnessed appeal.
variants.alternate: If the collector cannot be reached in time, lodge the dated appeal with an accountable office and preserve the receipt rather than physically confronting the collection party.
variants.failure: Unverified seizure or a falsely cleared debt leaves the accounts contested and the household at risk of further loss.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Timely review of a disputed arrears demand limits unrest caused by collecting an unproven balance.

variants.title: The Missing Register Leaf
variants.summary: A tax or dues account cannot be balanced because a register leaf has gone missing. Households dispute a demand that cannot yet be proven.
variants.dialogue: Ink is no proof when the page is gone. Hear the affected households before you enter another figure.
objectives: Compare the surviving receipts and register totals, marking the entries that cannot be substantiated.
Hear the disputed claim and enter only a supported correction with an accountable witness.
variants.alternate: If the missing entry cannot be reconstructed, suspend that disputed balance and preserve both claims for a later hearing rather than guessing an amount.
variants.failure: Inventing a lost figure or charging an unproven balance invalidates the correction and its reward.
variants.strategicAccomplishment: Documenting the missing evidence avoids imposing an unproven levy while an accountable correction is sought.

variants.title: The Boundary Without a Marker
variants.summary: A boundary stone is missing near a field both neighbors use. Neither claimant will accept a new permanent line without testimony.
variants.dialogue: The stone is gone, but the crops remain. Mark where each party agrees to work until the old line can be proved.
objectives: Survey visible boundary evidence and hear both neighbors' current use claims.
Record a witnessed interim arrangement that neither party is told amounts to a permanent title.
variants.alternate: If the old marker cannot be located, document a temporary use boundary with both claimants while leaving ownership unresolved.
variants.failure: Moving a marker secretly or claiming a permanent settlement without evidence voids the mediation.

variants.title: The Unsteady Scale
variants.summary: A market balance gives different readings for the same bale. A customer has paid for a full measure, and the vendor wants the error settled before handover.
variants.dialogue: The beam settles differently each time. I would sooner return a few coins than send someone away short-weighted.
objectives: Compare the stall's balance against an agreed reference weight and identify any difference.
Reweigh the purchased goods and correct the quantity or price with the buyer before completing the exchange.
variants.alternate: If no trustworthy reference weight is available, hold the sale and return the advance rather than certify a doubtful measure.
variants.failure: A disputed weighing cannot be accepted as a fully settled market exchange.

variants.title: The Two Marked Weights
variants.summary: Two traders produce weights carrying different marks, and each accuses the other of cheating. Local measures may differ, so a discrepancy alone is not proof of fraud.
variants.dialogue: His weight has one seal, mine another. Name the measure we agreed to before you name either of us a thief.
objectives: Record which local measure the traders agreed to use and compare both sets of weights against a neutral market reference.
Resolve the actual quantity and price with both parties, keeping the accusation separate from the observed discrepancy.
variants.alternate: If the disputed standard cannot be settled, suspend the weighed sale or negotiate a countable lot with both traders' consent.
variants.failure: The sale remains contested without a verified common measure; no fraud verdict is issued from conflicting marks alone.

variants.title: The Porters Are Waiting
variants.summary: A consignment is about to leave the market when its buyer notices that the loaded bales do not match the paid tally. There is still time to count them before the porters depart.
variants.dialogue: They have lifted the bales already, but the tally is wrong. Count them here before the road hides the mistake.
objectives: Count and inspect the outgoing bales while the consignment remains at the market.
Correct the invoice and delivered quantity with the buyer, or place the disputed load on hold before departure.
variants.alternate: If the full consignment cannot be assembled, obtain the buyer's consent to a delayed or reduced shipment with a written shortfall.
variants.failure: The uncorrected consignment cannot be certified as delivered in full.

variants.title: The Unfilled Bale Order
variants.summary: A trader cannot fill an agreed order from the remaining sound bales. A buyer fears being charged for weight that will never arrive.
variants.dialogue: Let us weigh what is actually on the floor, not what the old contract says should be there.
objectives: Inspect the sound goods and weigh what can still be supplied at the current market.
Offer the buyer a corrected quantity and price, then record the agreed exchange and receipt.
variants.alternate: If the original quantity is unavailable, renegotiate the order against weighed stock and disclose any change of grade or price before payment.
variants.failure: Hiding shortages, inferior grade or altered weights forfeits the trade commission.

variants.title: The Blocked Wagon Road
variants.summary: A damaged crossing has halted a small consignment. Carriers lack enough spare labor to repair the route quickly, and a detour might spoil the cargo.
variants.dialogue: I will not send a second wagon onto the same broken bridge. Mark a sound way before we move the first.
objectives: Inspect the obstruction and determine whether clearance or a safe detour is practical.
Guide one witnessed trial consignment through the chosen route and record the cargo's arrival and losses.
variants.alternate: If the crossing cannot be made safe, agree on a practicable detour and record added distance and losses rather than treating the road as cleared.
variants.failure: Sending carriers over a known unsafe crossing or inventing a successful delivery ends the route commission.

variants.title: The Absent Skiff
variants.summary: A small harbor craft has not returned after a shift in weather. The watch has a last sighting, but the crew's families have no verified account.
variants.dialogue: The watch saw their sail before dusk. I won't tell their families they are lost until someone checks.
objectives: Compare the watch's last reliable sighting with the crew's intended route; search safely for survivors or identifiable evidence.
Return survivors, or give their families a verified account of what the search found.
variants.alternate: If weather makes the approach unsafe, gather independent shore sightings and record the search as incomplete rather than claiming a rescue.
variants.failure: An abandoned search without reliable evidence remains unresolved; no rescue reward is paid.

variants.title: Two Accounts of the Missing Boat
variants.summary: Two crews disagree about why a harbor boat departed. One says its sailors volunteered; another says they were ordered out in worsening weather.
variants.dialogue: The cargo ledger says one thing; the harbor watch says another. Find where their accounts part.
objectives: Compare the harbor watch's departure record with the crew and cargo accounts.
Check the last known safe approach and return corroborated evidence without treating an accusation as fact.
variants.alternate: If the accounts remain irreconcilable, preserve both testimonies for an independent harbor authority instead of naming a culprit.
variants.failure: An unsupported accusation closes the inquiry without a reward; the disappearance remains unresolved.

variants.title: Before the Tide Turns
variants.summary: A vessel was last seen drifting toward an unsafe approach. The next tide could close the only reasonable search window.
variants.dialogue: We have one safe window before the tide turns. Do not send another boat into the same danger.
objectives: Confirm the last reported position and plan a safe search before the changing tide.
Aid any survivors and warn nearby crews, or return reliable evidence of what happened.
variants.alternate: If a safe search cannot launch in time, warn other crews and document the unfinished search for a later attempt.
variants.failure: When the safe window passes, the immediate rescue remains unresolved and the full rescue reward is forfeited.

variants.title: A Search Without a Launch
variants.summary: The harbor watch reports too few safe craft and crews to search every reported approach. Families need a search plan that does not endanger another crew.
variants.dialogue: I can lend a lantern and the pilot's notes. I cannot send another family to sea in an unsafe boat.
objectives: Inspect the available search craft and agree on a safe approach with local harbor crews.
Search the reachable route and return survivors or verifiable evidence to the waiting families.
variants.alternate: If no safe craft or guide is available, search the accessible shoreline and state clearly which waters remain unchecked.
variants.failure: Sending an unseaworthy craft or claiming an unchecked route was searched ends the task without reward.
